title: cmd_rect induction over commands proves the array-init pass preserves function equivalence
intent: Prove that the array-init pass (add_init_prog), which inserts array initialisation before first use, preserves whole-function equivalence wiequiv_f, by structural induction over the command language with cmd_rect; each command form is closed by one of three auxiliary lemmas, and the result plugs into the compiler's per-pass simulation chain.
also_known_as: structural induction over the command language

parent.name: it_add_init_callP
parent.statement: Lemma it_add_init_callP fn : wiequiv_f p p' ev ev (rpreF (eS:= eq_spec)) fn fn (rpostF (eS:=eq_spec)).

children.name: it_aux
children.statement:
Lemma it_aux I ii1 ii i :
  wequiv_rec p p' ev ev eq_spec (cmpl_inv I)
     [:: MkI ii i]
     (add_init ii1 I (Sv.union (write_i i) (read_i i)) (MkI ii i)) (cmpl_inv (Sv.union I (write_i i))).
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: adding the initialisation of a single instruction is equivalent

children.name: add_init_auxP
children.statement:
Lemma add_init_auxP ii c c' I I' X :
 disjoint I X ->
 wequiv_rec p p' ev ev eq_spec (cmpl_inv I) c c' (cmpl_inv I') ->
 wequiv_rec p p' ev ev eq_spec (cmpl_inv I) c (Sv.fold (add_init_aux ii) X c') (cmpl_inv I').
children.closed_by: elim over Sv.elements (line 164); apply wequiv_cat / wequiv_assign_right (lines 170-171)
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: folding add_init_aux over a disjoint variable set preserves equivalence

children.name: cmpl_inv_incl
children.statement: Lemma cmpl_inv_incl I1 I2 s1 s2 : Sv.Subset I1 I2 -> cmpl_inv I1 s1 s2 → cmpl_inv I2 s1 s2.
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the invariant cmpl_inv is monotone in the variable set

applicability.goal_shape: A compiler pass defined by recursion over a command/instruction syntax (add_init_i / add_init_c), proved equivalent by structural induction over that syntax via cmd_rect, with the invariant a state relation parameterised by a set of live variables (cmpl_inv I).
applicability.use_when: the pass is syntax-directed (its effect on each constructor is local), so the induction follows the definition; the invariant can be expressed as a relation indexed by a variable set; each constructor needs only a short lemma about its own effect.
applicability.avoid_when: the pass's effect is non-local (whole-program or global analysis) or the invariant is not indexable by syntax; the constructors need substantially different reasoning, so a shared dispatch like '1-4, 6-8: apply/it_aux' does not fit.

metrics.how_counted: the cmd_rect application in the parent yields 10 goals (nil, cons, and the 8 instruction constructors); the dispatch '1-4, 6-8' closes 7 of them via apply/it_aux (line 239), and the if-case (lines 240-253) uses add_init_auxP and cmpl_inv_incl

consequences: The induction creates one goal per command constructor (here 10: nil, cons, and the 8 instruction forms); the if-case additionally splits into two branch subgoals, each of which must weaken the invariant from the branch's variable set to the whole set — that is exactly what cmpl_inv_incl does. The '1-4, 6-8' dispatch assumes the seven non-branching constructors share one shape; a constructor whose init effect differs (for example one that reads and writes overlapping variables) would need its own lemma and would break the shared step.
